vision: Modou keeps the state of every project a building-product supplier is chasing. It reads the requests, tender packages and public documents behind each project and tells the team which ones are real and still open, who holds the budget, what exactly they would supply, and what changed since last week.

strategy.direction: Stop selling project discovery and sell the state of the projects a supplier already has. Build one reader for tender packages and requests that pulls out the supplier's own items, quantities and contradictions, put it inside a project file that stays current from public documents, and prove both in the 30-day pilot with one supplier on 20 to 50 existing projects. Run the same reader past three estimators in parallel, and let a price, not enthusiasm, decide by 11 December which of the two buyers Modou serves.
why: Five of sixteen supplier calls said finding projects is not the problem: one is drowning in leads, one does not miss projects, one has leads for years, one hears of projects before the database, and one boss calls project data nonsense.

Discovery is crowded and priced low: Cobouw Bouwberichten runs from 800 to 10,500 euros a year, De Mercuur from 798 a region, Building Radar already scores projects and names decision-makers, and one supplier runs its own signal bots for about 60 euros a month.

The E4 pains come after the lead: a quarter or a tenth of requests are viable, finding the responsible person takes about eight hours a week, and much of an account manager's week goes to asking whether the product is still specified.

Unreadable documents hurt both buyers: a profiles supplier skips tender requests without a take-off, a cladding maker asks every enquiry for its square metres, and estimators spend one to two days filtering a package of hundreds of PDFs.

It follows the venture's own recorded decisions: sell the memory, not the brain (19 September), the primary problem is knowledge of state (22 September), and the next milestone is a 30-day pilot on 20 to 50 existing projects (22 September).

The only E5 commitments are from suppliers: a sandwich panel supplier asked to be a test user and a facade solar maker agreed to test the MVP. The eleven estimator calls are three days old and hold no commitment yet.
The reader is the one piece both directions share, so building it first costs nothing if the evidence later picks the estimator.

sequence.step: Collect ten real tender packages and platform requests from two suppliers and five from estimators. Build reader v0: given a supplier's product rules, list its items, quantities and contradictions with page references. Target: at least 7 in 10 items found against a human take-off.

Start the 30-day pilot with one supplier, one product line and 20 to 50 existing projects: a project file per project with phase, is it real, budget holder or unknown, items to supply, and a weekly what changed. Targets: the rep confirms the state on at least 7 in 10 projects and Modou flags at least 3 changes before the rep knew.
In parallel, replay five past tenders each for three estimator firms through the reader, inside their Bluebeam or IBIS flow, and ask each for a paid pilot price.

Put the weekly brief into the CRM the pilot team already uses and test a price between the self-approval line of 5,000 euros a year and the Cobouw and Mercuur plans they know. Sign or lose the first paid pilot.
Decision review against the kill criteria: keep the supplier as the ICP, switch to estimators, or stop.
If continuing, add two suppliers and the award handover alert, and start recording which signals led to won projects.

notNow: A national feed of new project leads: Cobouw, De Mercuur and Building Radar already sell it, and the suppliers interviewed do not lack leads.
Automated outreach agents: suppliers already build them for about 60 euros a month, and one marketing manager said an agent makes contact feel fake.
Automatic labour pricing or a full estimating engine: estimators doubt it at E2, IBIS, Admicom and Bouwmakers hold the calculation, and one firm turned down two vendor pitches.
A rules and certificates framework for every Western European country: large, and no customer asked for it.
A multi-product rules engine: already deprioritised on 18 September; start with one product line.
The energy-storage vertical: the key signal is a private talk with the grid operator and congestion leads are a price fight.
3D visualisation of the build-up: one owner valued it only as a sales picture.
killCriteria: By 9 October the reader finds fewer than 6 in 10 of a supplier's items on real packages: drop the document layer and test state tracking alone.
By 6 November the pilot rep calls the project state wrong or stale on more than a third of projects, or opens the file in fewer than two of four weeks: stop the supplier track.
Public documents name the budget holder on fewer than a quarter of the pilot's projects: drop the decider promise and sell state and scope only.
By 4 December no supplier accepts a paid pilot at 300 euros a month or more while an estimator firm does: switch the ICP to estimators.
Neither buyer accepts a paid pilot by 4 December: stop building and return to discovery with the pilot data.
Building Radar or Cobouw ships per-project state tracking for Dutch suppliers at a similar price before the first paid pilot: narrow to the tender reader.
evidenceGaps: Nobody has named a price for Modou. The only anchors are a recalled 2,000 euros a month for Mercuur, a 4,360 euro yearly Cobouw quote, a 5,000 euro self-approval limit and 60 euro DIY bots. Ask for a price in every pilot conversation.
Whether public documents name the funder of private projects in the Netherlands: test on the pilot's 20 to 50 projects in the first two weeks.
Whether a supplier's reps will read a brief outside their CRM: the pilot tracks weekly opens.
Most supplier calls are one front-end seller per firm; only two budget owners have spoken. Interview the sales director at the pilot supplier before pricing.
The estimator evidence is three days old with no follow-up; the five-tender replays are the first real test.
VSI needs a recompile after the direction decision: hypothesis-state is empty, and icp-state marks contractor estimation as validated while venture.md describes suppliers.

patterns.title: Project databases sell volume; buyers complain about freshness and contacts
patterns.text: The Dutch incumbents sell access to many projects: Cobouw Bouwberichten claims more than 400,000 projects and prices from 800 to 10,500 euros a year, De Mercuur from 798 euros a region. In the calls, one supplier stopped using its Mercuur subscription and two called the price too high.

initiatives.title: Project file that keeps itself current
initiatives.summary: One file per project a supplier follows, filled from the supplier's own requests and from permits, tenders and council decisions: phase, is it real, budget holder or unknown, what the supplier would supply, and what changed this week.
initiatives.bet: We believe that giving a supplier's reps a project file that updates itself from public documents will replace the status calls and self-built checklists they rely on now. We will know when the pilot rep confirms the state on at least 7 in 10 of 20 to 50 projects and Modou flags at least 3 changes before the rep knew.
initiatives.problem: Reps spend much of the week asking architects and builders whether a project is still on and whether the product is still specified, and keep track with checklists and CRM reminders.
risks: Public documents may not change often enough for private projects, so the file looks stale. Measure how many of the pilot's projects produce any event in 30 days.
Reps may trust their network over a file and never open it. Track weekly opens from week one.
CRMs differ per firm (Dynamics, Zoho, Monday, SAP), and one CRM barely exports data. Start with a weekly email and a CSV into their CRM.
Building Radar or Cobouw add per-project tracking; the defence is the supplier's own items and requests in the file, which they do not hold.
initiatives.firstMove: From 28 September, take 20 of the pilot supplier's open projects, find every public document for each by hand, and write the file manually for two weeks. If fewer than half the projects show any change or source worth showing, stop before automating.

initiatives.title: Tender reader: the supplier's items out of any package
initiatives.summary: Upload or forward a tender package or platform request and get back only the supplier's own items, quantities, specified requirements and contradictions, each with the page it came from.
initiatives.bet: We believe that a supplier who sees its own items and quantities pulled out of a full specification will bid on requests it now skips, and that the same reader saves estimators the day or two they spend filtering. We will know when reader v0 finds at least 7 in 10 items against a human take-off on ten real packages, and two firms ask to run their next package through it.
initiatives.problem: Tender platforms send the whole specification without a take-off, so suppliers skip requests, and estimators open hundreds of PDFs one by one before they can start.
risks: Specscan, HELDR.AI and 12Build already read Dutch specifications; Modou must be better for a supplier's specific product, not in general.
Scanned drawings and inconsistent numbering may defeat extraction. Test on the messiest packages first.
Suppliers may not share real packages. Ask the two E5 partners for five each in the first week.
The supplier-side pain rests on one E4 firm and one E3 firm; the estimator side is stronger but a different buyer.
initiatives.firstMove: By 9 October, collect ten packages from the two committed suppliers and five from estimators, run reader v0 against a take-off a human did, and report recall, false items and the contradictions found with page references.

initiatives.title: Fit rules that sort every request
initiatives.summary: Let each supplier write down the thresholds it already applies by feel, such as minimum square metres per region, project value, sustainability ambition and phase, and apply them to every request and project automatically.
initiatives.bet: We believe that a fit verdict built from the supplier's own rules will cut the time spent triaging requests that were never viable. We will know when the pilot rep agrees with the verdict on 9 in 10 requests over four weeks.

risks: Requests often lack the square metres, which is exactly why reps ask; the reader must find area in the documents or the rule cannot fire.
Rules that are too strict hide small projects from a regular customer, which suppliers make exceptions for.
initiatives.firstMove: Write the fit rules of the pilot supplier in one session, then score its last 50 requests and compare with what the team actually pursued.

initiatives.title: Contradiction check for estimators
initiatives.summary: For facade and envelope estimators, list where the specification, drawings, details and fire requirements disagree, each with page and line, so the estimator reviews a few suspect points instead of everything.
initiatives.bet: We believe estimators will pay for a contradiction list that shortens their check of a package, without Modou pricing anything. We will know when three firms replay five past tenders each and one offers a paid pilot by 4 December.
initiatives.problem: What is drawn fails to comply nine times out of ten, details do not match sections, and the estimator re-engineers the build-up unpaid before quoting.
risks: A different buyer from the supplier, with entrenched tools (Bluebeam, IBIS, Admicom, Bouwmakers) and fatigue from AI vendors.
Two firms already work with other AI builders and will not start a second track.
US estimating tools are funded; HELDR.AI and Specscan already read Dutch documents.
initiatives.firstMove: Ask three estimator firms from the September calls for five past packages with their final quotes, run the reader, and compare its contradictions with the questions they actually sent.

initiatives.title: Record which signals led to won projects
initiatives.summary: From the first pilot, log for every project which event came first, what the rep did and whether the product was specified and ordered, so the fit rules and the brief learn from outcomes.
initiatives.bet: We believe outcome data on the pilot's projects will become the one asset generic AI tools and new entrants lack. We will know when 50 projects have a recorded outcome by March 2027.
initiatives.problem: Building Radar has years of outcome data and Modou has none, and suppliers cannot attribute samples or visits to projects.
risks: Construction cycles of one and a half to two years mean few outcomes within the pilot.
Reps may not record outcomes unless it is one click from the brief.
initiatives.firstMove: Add won, lost and still open to every project file from the first pilot week.

initiatives.title: National feed of new project leads
initiatives.summary: A Modou database of new construction projects across the Netherlands, scored for each supplier, as the original venture description proposed.
initiatives.bet: We believed suppliers would pay for earlier and better-scored project leads than Cobouw or De Mercuur provide.
initiatives.problem: The original problem statement: suppliers hear about projects too late or too early.
risks: Parked: five of sixteen supplier calls said lead supply is not their problem, the network beats paid feeds on timing, and Cobouw, De Mercuur and Building Radar already sell this from 798 euros a year.
Revisit only for suppliers of new or compliance-driven products with a thin network, where timing stays the wedge.
initiatives.firstMove: None now. Keep a list of suppliers with a thin network who say timing is their problem.

initiatives.title: Grid-operator signals for energy-storage sellers
initiatives.summary: Predict which companies will hit grid congestion or have an underused connection, from grid-operator publications, for battery and energy-management sellers.
initiatives.bet: We believed battery sellers would pay for early congestion signals.
initiatives.problem: Battery sellers prospect by hand, for example by scanning roofs for solar panels.
risks: Parked: the strongest signal, a company talking to its grid operator about its connection, is private; congestion leads are a price fight with a one in five to one in seven win rate; one buyer's boss dismisses project data.
Grid congestion stays useful inside the supplier project file as a reason a project may stall.
initiatives.firstMove: None now; use grid wait-list data only as a stall signal in project files.
